deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 1983-84 'pseudo-droites' notes need maps on possibly NON-orientable surfaces. An arrangement of pseudolines lives in the projective plane, and the previous page sketches Möbius-type pictures. On this page Grothendieck gives a combinatorial datum for such a map and builds its surface.

The datum:
(i) A combinatorial graph Γ = (S, \vec A, σ_0, ·): vertices S, oriented edges \vec A, reversal a ↦ ā, origin map.
(ii) For each vertex s, a polygonal (dihedral) structure on the star \vec A_s, the set of oriented edges issuing from s. This is a cyclic order up to reversal; the margin calls it a 'semi-orientation'.
(iii) Writing ω(\vec A_s) for the 2-element set (torsor) of orientations of that polygon, transport isomorphisms φ_a : ω(\vec A_s) → ω(\vec A_t) for each a : s → t. The only condition is φ_ā = φ_a^{-1}.

For vertices of order 1 or 2 the polygon structure does not produce the 2-element set ω_s canonically. One must then supply it directly ('a datum of two orientations'). He therefore assumes all orders are ≥ 3 for simplicity, while noting that ν_s = 1, 2 is not excluded later.

In modern terms this is a generalized rotation system / signed rotation system / 'embedding scheme' with edge signs. Here the signs are packaged invariantly as a Z/2-torsor-valued local system on Γ, instead of ±1 labels relative to arbitrary chosen local orientations.

Construction of the surface:
- For each s, take the canonical topological realization Dis_s of the polygon DUAL to \vec A_s. Its sides α_a correspond to the elements a ∈ \vec A_s, i.e. to edges of Γ at s.
- Realize it via the barycentric subdivision, so Dis_s is a union of 2ν_s triangles indexed by the flags of \vec A_s.
- For each a : s → t, glue side α_a of Dis_s to side α_ā of Dis_t by an affine map. This map is determined by a bijection of endpoints, fixed by the rule: if ω_s and ω_t correspond under φ_a, the identification ψ_a must REVERSE the boundary orientations induced by ω_s and ω_t.

The next page states the result is a compact connected surface in which |Γ| embeds: vertex s is the barycentre of Dis_s, and edge a crosses α_a. So the vertices of Γ become 2-cells, and Γ is embedded as the dual graph of the polygon tiling. The figure shows exactly this: green polygons, the yellow dual graph Γ, flags hatched, a brown link circle round a vertex, and arrows marking ω_s, ω_t.

The next page then encodes the resulting map by flags (a, ω) with involutions σ_0, σ_1, σ_2, i.e. the cartographic group of Esquisse. Face rotation is ρ_f = σ_2σ_0, and vertex rotation is the usual polygon rotation on each Rep(\vec A_s).
errors: No mathematical error. The gluing rule (reverse the induced orientations when the local orientations correspond under φ_a) is the right one for consistency.
Gap: for vertices of order 1 or 2 the extra datum is only sketched (a 2-element orientation set with no polygon structure determining it). The text is heavily corrected here.
Gap: connectedness and compactness (stated on the next page) need Γ to be finite and connected.

Gap: the orientability criterion is not stated. The surface is orientable iff the Z/2-torsor local system (ω_s, φ_a) admits a global section, i.e. the associated 1-cocycle is a coboundary. This is implicit.

ideas.what: Encoding a (possibly non-orientable) map by a graph with dihedral structure on each vertex star plus transport isomorphisms between the 2-element orientation torsors along edges (φ_ā = φ_a^{-1}).
ideas.modern_name: generalized rotation system / signed rotation system / generalized embedding scheme (edge signatures); here phrased as a Z/2-torsor local system on Γ
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1970s), Stahl (Generalized embedding schemes, 1978); edge-signature formalism in Gross–Tucker, Mohar–Thomassen
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) treats maps via the cartographic group, oriented and non-oriented, but not this graph-plus-transport formulation as far as I know

ideas.what: Building the surface by gluing barycentrically realized polygons Dual(\vec A_s) along sides via orientation-reversing affine maps fixed by φ_a; Γ appears as the dual graph.
ideas.modern_name: surface realization of a ribbon/fat graph (dual polygon gluing), flag (barycentric) triangulation
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Heffter, Edmonds, Ringel; Jones–Singerman 1978 for flag-based realization)
ideas.where_published: close in spirit to Esquisse §3 (cartes and barycentric subdivision)

ideas.what: Treating orientations as a 2-element torsor ω(\vec A_s), functorial in \vec A_s, so that orientability is a torsor-triviality question.
ideas.modern_name: orientation local system / orientation double cover of a map
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (orientation sheaf; orientable double cover of maps)

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, torsor-flavoured but standard reformulation of signed rotation systems and the gluing construction of the associated surface. It is preparatory for the cartographic-group description of non-orientable maps needed for pseudoline arrangements in RP^2. Nothing here goes beyond the known theory of generalized embedding schemes and maps.
transcription_corrections: The parenthesis after 'avec une ... orientation' most likely reads '(structure polygonale donnée sur l'ens. des arêtes issues d'un sommet donné)', not 'l'un des sommets issus d'une orientation donnée'. The 'semi-orientation' wording is uncertain.
Figure labels read as 'η_s', 'η_t' are more plausibly 'ω_s', 'ω_t' (the local orientation arrows), together with '\vec a', 's', 't'.
'conséquemment plongée' on the next page is probably 'canoniquement plongée'.
